chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Las Vegas rooms: the Tropicana for Maynard Sloate and the Sands for Trotta
summary: People in Vegas accept him as jazz; he calls working the Sands for Trotta the delight of his life and describes the Tropicana trio.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: But see I'd worked there two and half years with a trio. I went in for three weeks at the Tropicana --
Yeah?

-- and for Maynard Sloat, he said you're this room the one to open the show. For some reason or other, the people in Vegas, having worked there for like 20 years or more, seem to accept me as a jazz thing there.
Oh.
I don't overdo it, I -- I think I don't go too loud and try -- I don't go for any championships or DownBeat poll awards or anything else --
Yeah.
Just do the job that I have to do and they never say anything to wat I play.
Yeah.
I found working at the Sands for Trotta was the delight time of my life, that was wonderful.
Yeah.
And he never said boo, and every once in a while he'd come around and say, "Is everything all right?" I'd say, "Fine," that's all there'd be to it.
Yeah.

And I found at the other hotels it was the same way, so when I went in for Maynard, this little room in the Tropicana, we went in for three weeks. And I'd been working on -- oh, around the world with George Wean Williams, so I didn't really know men (unintelligible). Who was around. So I finally -- most the guys I wanted to get were busy or something. I remember a guitar clarinet player I'd heard in Phoenix, and a Monk Montgomery who was with the Montgomery Brothers, was in San Francisco, so I hired him. I said drive to Vegas, and they drove and we opened Friday night, with no rehearsal or nothing. They got there Friday afternoon --
For heaven's sake.
-- and we went to work that night, for three weeks --
After you'd laid off for two years?
-- and we stayed two years, over two years. What?
After you had laid off, two years?
No, I -- this was before -- this was after I'd come back to work.
Oh, I see.
And this is before I laid off -- this is for -- four years, this is before.
Yeah, I see.
